parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no border/screening exposure documented, no organised targeting or documented trans-specific violence, and courts show a functioning record of pro-trans rulings (2023 bathroom ruling, sterilisation struck down). Friction is real but moderate: gender-segregated bathhouses with only guidance-level workarounds, no anti-discrimination statute, and a 2023 'understanding promotion' law without individual rights. The heaviest documented negative is custody practice: birth-sex/family-register placement with documented harm (bar-association warning, 2024 detention of a trans activist among men with initial HRT denial and mockery) — a tier-1 exposure only when detained, which is not a universal visitor exposure. Detention is a known adverse environment, bathhouse friction and thin recourse are moderate negatives; social reservedness plus visitor guides record ordinary tourist acceptance. Extrapolating thin axes from rule-of-law governance and no enforcement history, this sits at reduced risk, above 0.65 profiles with active unremedied universal exclusions, below 0.85 profiles with documented visitor-facing protections.
